title: The Golden Dome Proposal is Destabilizing and Dangerous
gist: Second of a two-part series arguing the Golden Dome missile defense proposal cannot effectively defend against long-range ballistic missiles yet would accelerate the nuclear arms race, provoke space weaponization and ASAT responses, compress crisis decision times to tens of seconds via boost-phase intercept, and destabilize via 'left of launch' doctrine. Authors argue arms control, not defense, is the only historically proven way to reduce nuclear threat, especially after New START limits lapsed in February 2026.

themes.theme: Golden Dome is ineffective yet escalatory

insights.claim: There is no prospect of building an effective defense against long-range ballistic missiles for the foreseeable future, and even a system that looks remotely effective on paper would cost hundreds of billions to trillions of dollars.
insights.speaker: Frederick Lamb and Laura Grego
insights.so_what: Golden Dome budget scale implies massive defense/space spending but questionable delivery; program risk is high.

insights.claim: An ineffective missile defense can still make the U.S. less safe because adversaries react to perceived future capability and a program of record with a budget in the hundreds of billions, by deploying more warheads and countermeasures.

insights.so_what: Golden Dome likely accelerates adversary nuclear and counterspace buildup — a structural arms-race driver.

themes.theme: Arms control as the proven alternative

insights.claim: The ABM Treaty and successive arms reduction treaties cut U.S. and Russian nuclear weapons from about 70,000 in the mid-1980s to about 8,000 today — the only large reduction in nuclear threat since nuclear weapons were first deployed.
insights.speaker: Frederick Lamb and Laura Grego
insights.so_what: Arms control is the only historically proven risk reducer; its collapse is a structural negative.

insights.claim: The failure to extend or replace New START, constrain Chinese forces, or limit tactical warheads, missile defenses and space weapons is increasing the nuclear threat and the risk of nuclear war.
insights.speaker: Frederick Lamb and Laura Grego
insights.so_what: Absence of any arms control framework elevates long-run geopolitical tail risk.
